Subject: Azure private plan — certification, data residency & purge terms

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the draft of the private plan listing — we've started an internal review and have a couple of gating items before legal/procurement can sign off. High level:

- We need Microsoft certification proof for the marketplace private offer (any certificate IDs or marketplace attestation you can provide).
- Data residency: our customers are EU-based and require Germany (DE) residency for retained logs and data. Can you confirm deployment boundaries and whether you can commit to DE storage for customer data?
- Data purge/retention: our standard is ability to request deletion with a 30-day purge window and evidence of deletion/audit logs. We see your draft currently references a 90-day window. Is there flexibility here?

If you can share the SOC2 attestation and a redline showing the proposed language for purge / residency, procurement can take this to our legal. We're on a tight timeline for our go-live on Nov 1, so prompt responses will help.

Attaching the marketplace checklist from our side (not attached here).

Thanks,
Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the checklist and callout. Quick responses inline and attachments below.

- Marketplace certification: attaching our SOC2 Type II (2025) attestation and a sandbox listing link where Microsoft verifies the private offer metadata. We also have a Microsoft Marketplace validation ticket (ID: MSFT-98721) and can provide the attestation letter if needed.
- Data residency: our Private deployments (VPC/on-prem option) support region pinning. For the hosted private plan we can guarantee Azure region West Europe (Netherlands) or Germany West Central; the preferred option for DE residency is Germany West Central. We will document deployment boundaries in the Azure listing and in the SOW.
- Data purge/retention: understood — your 30-day expectation is noted. Our default hosted private-plan draft used a 90-day retention window for backups and for a safety buffer on customer support investigations. We can propose a compromise: a 30-day hard-delete API and a 90-day disaster-recovery snapshot retention where snapshots are encrypted and isolated, with an auditable justification flow for any snapshot retention beyond 30 days (requires joint approval).

I've attached: redwood-azure-private-plan-draft-20260830.pdf and SOC2_Type2_attestation_2025.pdf. Looping in Neha from Legal to propose concrete language.

Next steps: Neha — can you review the compromise language below and provide a redline we can send to Northern Fintech legal?

Best,
Aisha

Elena / Aisha — thanks for the context. I reviewed the draft and added a tracked-redline (attached) with proposed contractual language. Key items we recommend and what we can concede:

1) Data residency: we will contractually commit that all Production customer data collected/stored through the hosted private plan for Northern Fintech customers will be provisioned in Germany West Central. The Contract will include an exhibit listing the Azure regions and the deployment control process.

2) Data deletion / purge: Our proposed language (summary):
- Customer Data Deletion API: Redwood will implement and maintain an API allowing Northern Fintech to request deletion of Customer Data.
- Deletion window: Redwood will execute deletion within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of a verified deletion request, subject to (a) any active legal hold and (b) a 7-day reconciliation buffer for in-flight requests.
- Snapshots & backups: Redwood will segregate disaster recovery snapshots; these will be destroyed within ninety (90) calendar days unless a joint written exception is approved by both parties. Any retention >30 days will require documented justification and exportability of the retained data to Northern Fintech upon request.
- Evidence & audit logs: Redwood will provide deletion confirmation and audit entries (time, actor, change token) within five (5) business days of completion.

3) Certification & attestation: We can provide SOC2 Type II attestation and Microsoft marketplace validation confirmation. For compliance teams that require runtime attestations we can provide periodic compliance attestations and a redacted architecture diagram. We cannot grant unrestricted access to our internal monitoring systems, but we will support an agreed SOC2 review and provide Azure marketplace artifacts.

I've attached the redline (redline_legal_comments_20260830.docx) and put suggested wording into Section 7 (Data Protection & Deletion). Please review and let me know any specific additions Northern Fintech requires.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Elena — appreciate the thorough review and the timeline. On behalf of Commercial and Product, we're comfortable with Neha's proposed compromise:

- We will commit to Germany West Central for Northern Fintech production deployments in contract exhibit.
- We accept the 30-day deletion API execution window (with the 7-day reconciliation buffer and legal hold carve-out).
- Snapshots will be handled as Neha described with a documented exception process.

Operational items: Aisha, please confirm engineering ETA to expose the deletion API and the export capability (we need realistic timelines for their procurement team). Once we have an agreed redline, I'll approve a one-time concession in the commercial SOW to include the DE region and subscription mapping.

Elena — if this meets procurement's needs, we'll prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW and a redline for Northern Fintech legal. Target to have this signed by mid-September to meet your Nov 1 go-live.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
